artifacts.title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found that Great Lakes Presbytery erred in declaring TE Gonzales's second complaint out of order by conflating it with the first complaint (SJC 2010-28), but denied the complaint on the merits because TE Dupee's allegedly offending statement was made in his representative capacity as Committee Chairman, not personally, and therefore could not be the subject of a BCO 31-2 investigation.

artifacts.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery was found to have erred in restoring deposed minister A. B. Scott to the office of Teaching Elder by a vote of 19-17, which the SJC determined did not satisfy the BCO 34-8 requirement that 'the general sentiment of the Church is strongly in his favor.' The SJC annulled NFP's actions and remanded the case; a lengthy dissent by RE Donahoe argued that BCO 34-8 does not require a super-majority and that the restoration vote is distinct from the evaluation of general sentiment.

artifacts.synopsis: Identical companion case to 2011-03; the SJC denied this complaint by TE Grover Gunn et al. against Covenant Presbytery's handling of its MNA Committee report on the same grounds as 2011-03, with both cases heard together by an expanded panel.

artifacts.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

artifacts.synopsis: Harry Long and others complained that James River Presbytery erred by instructing ordained TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views on creation days after granting him an exception. The SJC denied the complaint, deferring to the Presbytery's discretion, with a dissent arguing that the liberty of conscience principles and prior GA decisions made the instruction to Conrad inappropriate.

artifacts.title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.

artifacts.title: Review and control action while a judicial case is pending on appeal

matches.evidence: A higher court may note an exception through review and control but may take no action on it while judicial proceedings are pending; the effect of any unconstitutional act is suspended upon appeal.

artifacts.title: Proper use of memorials and finality of adjudicated GA decisions

matches.evidence: A memorial under BCO 40-5 is the proper recourse for alleging GA error after adjournment; the Assembly will not reopen a finally adjudicated case except to correct a manifest error.

artifacts.title: Notice of complaint sufficiency and timing of suspension motion under BCO 43-4

matches.evidence: Northeast Presbytery asked whether a written statement of intent to complain constitutes adequate notice to suspend a court's action and when a suspension motion is procedurally in order.

artifacts.title: Recourse when General Assembly may have erred in a decision

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that errors alleged during a GA meeting may be challenged under BCO 45, and subsequent assemblies may take contrary positions but cannot annul prior actions.

artifacts.title: Scope and duration of BCO debate prohibitions during a complaint

matches.evidence: BCO prohibitions on debate apply only to the specific matter complained, only until final adjudication, and to all members of the lower court — expiring upon final resolution.
